threads.body: The Bedrock invoke_agent span name is still the generic "invoke_agent" even though other agent scenarios in this PR switched to the "<operation> <agent identifier>" pattern (e.g., azure-ai-foundry/scenario.py:110-112, openai-assistants/scenario.py:105-107). For consistency with the updated convention and to make traces easier to scan, include the invoked agent identifier in the span name here as well.

threads.body: This route is declared with a trailing slash ("/agents/"). If the boto3 client sends a request to "/agents" (no trailing slash), Flask will respond with a redirect that botocore may not follow for a PUT request, causing the scenario to fail. Declaring the route without a trailing slash (or setting strict_slashes=False) avoids redirect behavior and makes the mock more robust.

threads.body:
Not sure about this AI claim, but passing it along:

Agent Engine isn't part of the deprecation, so "SDK deprecated" is the wrong reason here. The banner right above lists the deprecated modules and `vertexai.agent_engines` isn't one of them — `google-cloud-aiplatform` 2.0.0, which this scenario already pins, still documents `client.agent_engines.create(...)` as a supported surface. Since this PR is a survey of where `create_agent` applies, I'd rather this row said it's simply not implemented, otherwise a real remaining gap gets written off.

```suggestion
| create_agent / invoke_agent (client) | Yes — Agent Engine (`vertexai.agent_engines`, not deprecated) hosts agents remotely | ❌ Not implemented |
```
